title: The Roll Down Gate
story: The gate rolls down at ten and the night shift of painters clocks in. One masterpiece burner over years of tags, the streetlight raking every ridge

title: The Night Vet
story: The 3am animal ER, a cat's paw bandaged while its human cries with relief. One recovering pigeon in a shoebox marked with a heart, mercy running the night shift

title: The Steps Lunch
story: A hundred sandwiches at the feet of five thousand years of art. The pigeons work the crowd like docents collecting dues

title: The Fool
story: He steps off the bus with one suitcase and total faith, a bodega cat at his heels. The skyline is the cliff he cannot see, and he will survive it

title: The Steps
story: A thousand cameras fire and she turns around to see the crowd instead. The museum steps, limestone gold, a gown blooming all the way down

title: The Docent of Forgotten Donors
story: She reads the small brass names aloud and the named arrive. A monthly tour for four hundred generosities, her voice the only thing keeping them warm

title: Vladan Novotny, a night nurse holding a floor alone
story: Holding an entire floor alone is not heroism, it is a staffing decision. Bed to chair, one careful lift, a phone face down on the tray

title: Leah Teitelbaum, a night companion paid to simply be awake in a house
story: Being awake is the entire job, and it is harder than it sounds. Four in the morning, a notebook of times and doses, a strange lamp

title: Fitzroy Bonaparte, a night nurse holding a floor alone
story: Endurance keeps getting mistaken for a plan on the night shift. Two minutes in the stairwell, hands cracked, a tube of cream in the pocket

title: Choden Sarmiento, a respite worker who gets four hours to be a person
story: Four hours is what the city allocates for a family to breathe. Called the daughter by a neighbour, she nods and picks up the transfer belt

title: Halima Achebe, a dementia care specialist who plays one song every day
story: Music reaches a place the medication has never once found. She sings the same song quietly into a room with no answer

title: Arjun Rahman, a doula who has delivered on four bathroom floors
story: Four bathroom floors, four first breaths, and no line on any certificate. Mistaken for a cousin at the door, he lets it stand and carries the bag
